about: The operating model of the agentic team (Dinis with Angelo, in architect.1's session, 14:40 UTC; briefs/2026-11-11-1440-the-operating-model.md; work/48): the primitives of the execution block, the access an entity has at a moment in time, identity, state, providers, and who can do what. What an entity is depends on where it runs and what it can reach (Dinis: 'what they are depends on where they are and what they can do'). A draft for Dinis and Angelo to correct.

ladder.about: The execution ladder: what an entity can do, bottom to top. Each rung includes the ones below it.

rungs.name: compute
rungs.what: raw code execution: a script, a build, a CI job

rungs.name: model call
rungs.what: a prompt in, an answer out (the first chatbots)
rungs.example: the second opinion via the router

rungs.name: loop
rungs.what: a simple agentic workflow: the model's output feeds its next step, without tools
rungs.example: a chain of calls in one script

rungs.name: loop with tools
rungs.what: the loop can act: shell, files, web, git
rungs.example: a Claude Code session; a ChatGPT agent

rungs.name: schedules
rungs.what: it can wake itself later (create and keep schedules)

rungs.name: spawn
rungs.what: it can start new agents, sessions and environments: the control plane

across: tools (what the loop can touch: tools appear at E3 but a call can also be given tools)
storage (what it can mount: a file system, git, vaults)

access.about: The capabilities an entity has at a moment in time: what it can reach and change. Each axis has levels; 'who' below gives each runtime's level today.

levels: create (make its own vaults: its own record)
sessions, schedules, environments, credentials (Claude's control plane)

identity.rule: Every entity has an identity: a PKI key, even a chat session where it can carry one (Dinis: 'our identities have to flow to everything here').
identity.ephemeral: A session key's private half lives only as long as its session. That is a feature: a signature by it proves the agent existed at that moment (Dinis: 'that tells you that that agent exists at that moment in time').
how: pki-agent.mjs keygen --session in each session; the public half in data/keys.json
every output signed: commits (the Agent: trailer and the key), inbox messages, agent-log runs, vault records
a chat (S1) can be given a key by the person who runs it, and sign what it returns through that person's tool

state.about: How state reaches a model and leaves it.

carriers.holds: evidence, captures, any state; easy to distribute, even as a zip
carriers.provenance: made by one session: that session's record
the provider's; never the only copy

carriers.holds: a task, its inputs and where the output goes, signed
carriers.provenance: the lead's signature; the doer signs its output

providers.models: open weight (DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen) and others, image models included

os.about: Read as a distributed operating system (Dinis: 'almost like ... a distributed operating system ... we decouple ... who's actually doing the task').

map.here: the control plane: sessions, schedules, wakes, spawn (E4, E5)
git and vaults (zips to move them)
signed inboxes and append lanes; task packets
install: npm, pip, apt where allowed
the ABP hook log, the router's ledger, agent-log runs

who.about: Each runtime or entity with its rung and its access today (from data/runtimes.json and the environments as seen in this swarm).

items.identity: none; the calling agent signs the result

items.vault: through a person (L0) or a link
items.identity: none today; proposed: the person's tool signs
a key given to it, or the person's

items.entity: A Claude Code cloud agent (R1), e.g. design.1

graph.about: Read as a graph (Dinis's 'meaning through connectivity'): every entity is a node, and what it is comes from its edges: runs-on (a runtime), uses (a model), reaches (git, a vault, a host), holds (a key), may (its ABP grant), does (a task). The same pattern repeats at every scale: a call inside an agent, an agent inside a team, a team inside the swarm.

open: Dinis's 'thinking in graphs' text on fractal semantic graphs: to read once linked
whether tools are a rung (E3) or an axis across rungs (Dinis: 'maybe tools is transversal')
